copy.bis: Ang mikrobyo mahimong mabuhi sa mga kaptanan sa pultahan ug uban pang butang nga gihikapan sa daghang tawo.

copy.en:
Why is soap so good at fighting germs?

Soap breaks apart germs on your hands and makes it hard for them to hold on, so they rinse away with water — that's why washing for 20 seconds works so well!
copy.tl:
Bakit epektibo ang sabon laban sa germs?

Sinisira ng sabon ang germs sa kamay at pinapahirapan silang kumapit, kaya naaanod sila sa tubig — kaya epektibo ang paghuhugas nang 20 segundo!
copy.bis:
Nganong epektibo ang sabon batok sa germs?

Ginaguba sa sabon ang germs sa kamot ug lisod na sila makapyot, mao nga mahugasan sila sa tubig — mao nga maayo ang paghugas og 20 segundos!

copy.tl: Ang bakuna ay nagtuturo sa depensa ng katawan na kilalanin ang mikrobyo nang maaga, kaya kapag dumating ang totoong sakit, handa na itong labanan.
copy.bis: Ang bakuna nagtudlo sa depensa sa lawas nga mailhan ang kagaw nga sayo, busa kon moabot ang tinuod nga sakit, andam na kini nga makigbatok.

copy.tl: Ang ghost crab ay isang maputlang alimasag na naninirahan sa lungga sa buhangin at mabilis na tumatakbo tuwing gabi para maghanap ng pagkain.
copy.bis: Ang ghost crab usa ka maputi nga kasag nga nagpuyo sa lungag sa balas ug paspas modagan sa gabii aron mangita ug pagkaon.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions algae living inside the clam, which hints at an interaction, but it does not explain how the living things depend on one another or on the environment to meet basic needs. It only explains the source of the clam's color.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food

copy.en:
Why is a giant clam so colorful?

A giant clam's fleshy mantle glows blue, green, or gold when open — the colors come from tiny algae living inside it.
copy.tl:
Bakit makukulay ang taklobo?

Ang laman ng taklobo ay kumikinang na asul, berde, o ginto kapag nakabukas — nagmumula ang kulay sa mga lumot na naninirahan sa loob nito.
copy.bis:
Nganong mabulokon ang taklobo?

Ang unod sa taklobo mosidlak og asul, lunhaw, o bulawan kon naabli — gikan ang kolor sa mga lumot nga nagpuyo sa sulod niini.

copy.en: The giant panda has black and white fur, with black patches circling its eyes.
copy.tl: May itim at puting balahibo ang giant panda, na may itim na bilog sa palibot ng mga mata nito.
copy.bis: Ang giant panda adunay itom ug puti nga balhibo, nga adunay itom nga libot sa mga mata niini.

copy.en:
How long can a giant panda live?

A giant panda can live about 20 years in the wild, and even longer when cared for in a zoo!
copy.tl:
Gaano katagal nabubuhay ang giant panda?

Ang giant panda ay maaaring mabuhay nang mga 20 taon sa kagubatan, at mas matagal pa sa zoo!
copy.bis:
Unsa kadugay mabuhi ang giant panda?

Ang giant panda makabuhi og mga 20 ka tuig sa kalasangan, ug mas dugay pa sa zoo!

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions an animal's age but does not use a flow chart or compare life-cycle stages, so it does not directly support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Jonathan, a giant tortoise, is over 190 years old

assignedReviews.reason: The card is about an animal's age, not about growth, response, or reproduction, so it only shares the broad topic of living things.

copy.en:
Who is the oldest known land animal alive today?

Jonathan, a giant tortoise, is over 190 years old — the oldest living land animal known.
copy.tl:
Sino ang kilalang pinakamatandang hayop sa lupa?

Si Jonathan, isang higanteng pagong, ay mahigit 190 taong gulang — ang pinakamatandang buhay na hayop sa lupa na kilala.
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang giila nga pinakatigulang nga hayop sa yuta?

Si Jonathan, usa ka dakong bao, kapin na sa 190 ka tuig — ang pinakatigulang buhi nga hayop sa yuta nga giila.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Giant tortoises can live more than 100 years
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses lifespan, not life-cycle stages, and does not use a flow chart or compare stages. It shares the animal topic but provides no instructional support for comparing life cycles.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce

copy.en:
How long can a giant tortoise live?

Giant tortoises can live more than 100 years, making them one of the longest-living animals on Earth!
copy.tl:
Gaano katagal mabuhay ang giant tortoise?

Ang giant tortoise ay kayang mabuhay nang mahigit 100 taon, kaya isa ito sa pinakamatagal mabuhay na hayop sa mundo!
copy.bis:
Unsa kadugay mabuhi ang giant tortoise?

Ang giant tortoise makabuhi og kapin sa 100 ka tuig, mao nga usa kini sa labing dugay mabuhi nga mananap sa kalibutan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In a gibbous moon, more than half, but not all, of the Moon's face is beautifully lit!

copy.en:
How much of the Moon is lit during a gibbous moon?

In a gibbous moon, more than half, but not all, of the Moon's face is beautifully lit!
copy.tl:
Gaano karami ang maliwanag sa gibbous moon?

Sa gibbous moon, mahigit kalahati, pero hindi pa buo, ng mukha ng Buwan ang naliliwanagan!
copy.bis:
Pila ka daghan ang hayag sa gibbous moon?

Sa gibbous moon, kapin sa katunga, apan dili pa tibuok, sa nawong sa Bulan ang nahayagan!

copy.bis: Samtang nagaagos ang tubig sa hasang, gikuha niini ang oksiheno nga natunaw sa tubig ug gipasulod diretso sa dugo.

copy.en: Ginger is grown all over the Philippines and used in favorite dishes like tinola and ginger tea, called salabat.
copy.tl: Ang luya ay laganap na itinatanim sa Pilipinas at ginagamit sa mga lutuin tulad ng tinola at salabat.
copy.bis: Ang luy-a kaylap nga gitanom sa Pilipinas ug gigamit sa mga pagkaon sama sa tinola ug salabat.

copy.en: Male giraffes fight by swinging their long necks and slamming them against each other!
copy.tl: Ang mga lalaking dyirap ay nag-aaway sa pamamagitan ng paghampas ng kanilang mahabang leeg sa isa't isa!
copy.bis: Ang lalaki nga giraffe nag-away pinaagi sa paghapak sa ilang taas nga liog sa usag-usa!

assignedReviews.reason: Neck-bone count is not muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory as a set.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the differences between animals with a backbone (vertebrates) and animals without backbones (invertebrates) by using common local examples of each group
assignedReviews.reason: Giraffe and human neck bones are two vertebrates, not backbone versus no backbone.

copy.en:
How many neck bones does a giraffe have?

Even with its super long neck, a giraffe has only seven neck bones — the same number as a human!
copy.tl:
Ilang buto ang nasa leeg ng dyirap?

Kahit napakahaba ng leeg nito, pitong buto lang ang nasa leeg ng dyirap — kapareho ng tao!
copy.bis:
Pila ka bukog ang naa sa liog sa giraffe?

Bisan taas kaayo ang liog niini, pito ra ka bukog ang naa sa liog sa giraffe — pareho sa tawo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: you can see them in safari parks like Calauit in Palawan
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions an animal and a place (safari park) but does not use a drawing or diagram to classify Philippine animals/plants by habitat (terrestrial/aquatic/aerial). Giraffes are not native Philippine animals, and no classification is attempted.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: you can see them in safari parks like Calauit in Palawan
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a list or draw up a table with examples of animals and plants in a particular habitat, such as a garden, rice field, seashore, and mangrove swamp

Where can you see giraffes in the Philippines?

Giraffes don't live wild in the Philippines, but you can see them in safari parks like Calauit in Palawan.
copy.tl:
Saan makikita ang dyirap sa Pilipinas?

Hindi nakatira ang dyirap sa Pilipinas, ngunit makikita ito sa mga safari park gaya ng Calauit sa Palawan.
copy.bis:
Asa makita ang giraffe sa Pilipinas?

Wala magpuyo nga ihalas ang giraffe sa Pilipinas, apan makita kini sa mga safari park sama sa Calauit sa Palawan.

Why is glass clear?

Its atoms are arranged in a jumbled, non-crystal way, so it doesn't scatter the light passing through!
copy.tl:
Bakit malinaw ang bubog?

Dahil ang mga atomo nito ay nakaayos nang magulo, hindi tulad ng kristal, kaya hindi nito kinakalat ang liwanag!
copy.bis:
Nganong tin-aw ang bildo?

Tungod kay ang mga atomo niini magubot ang pagkahan-ay, dili sama sa kristal, mao nga dili niini magkatag ang kahayag!

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions particle arrangement in glass but does not use diagrams or illustrations, does not address spacing or relative motion, and does not describe the three states of matter. assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe sources of light and their use in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why light passes through glass, but it does not describe sources of light or their use in everyday situations. The light transmission is a consequence of glass structure, not a description of light sources or uses.

copy.en:
Why is glass clear even though it is made from sand?

When it cools quickly, its tiny parts don't line up neatly like a crystal. This messy pattern lets light pass right through!
copy.tl:
Bakit malinaw ang salamin kahit gawa ito sa buhangin?

Kapag mabilis itong pinalamig, hindi nagkakahanay nang maayos ang maliliit na bahagi nito. Dahil dito, nakakadaan ang liwanag!
copy.bis:
Ngano klaro ang salamin bisan hinimo gikan sa balas?

Kung paspas mapalamig, ang gagmay nga bahin niini dili maayos og pagkahan-ay. Tungod ani, makaagi ang kahayag!

copy.tl: Ang lumilipad na butiki, lumulutang na ahas, at lumulutang na tuko ay hindi magkamag-anak, ngunit magkahiwalay silang natutong lumutang.
copy.bis: Ang naglupad nga tiki, naglutaw nga halas, ug naglutaw nga tiki dili suod nga paryente, apan tagsa-tagsa sila nga nakakat-on molutaw.

assignedReviews.reason: The card provides descriptive information about gneiss but does not teach classification using a simple rock classification system or dichotomous key, nor does it compare multiple rock samples.

copy.en: Gneiss is a high-grade metamorphic rock with alternating light and dark bands. It forms under extreme pressure and heat at the deepest roots of mountain ranges!
copy.tl: Ang gneiss ay isang high-grade metamorphic rock na may alternating na maliwanag at madilim na mga band. Nabubuo ito sa ilalim ng matinding presyon at init sa pinakamalalim na ugat ng mga bulubundukin!
copy.bis: Ang gneiss usa ka high-grade metamorphic rock nga adunay alternating nga hayag ug ngitngit nga mga banda. Naporma kini ilalom sa grabe nga presyon ug init sa pinaka-lalum nga mga gamot sa mga bukid!

Where does the body store extra energy?

Extra energy from go foods gets stored in the liver and muscles for later — like saving battery power for your next game.
copy.tl:
Saan itinatago ng katawan ang sobrang lakas?

Ang sobrang lakas mula sa go food ay itinatago ng katawan sa atay at kalamnan para gamitin mamaya — parang baterya na inimbak para sa susunod na laro.
copy.bis:
Asa gitipigan sa lawas ang sobra nga kusog?

Ang sobra nga kusog gikan sa go food gitipigan sa lawas sa atay ug unod aron magamit unya — sama sa pagtipig og baterya para sa sunod nga duwa.

copy.tl: Maraming Pilipino ang nag-aalaga ng kambing sa bakuran dahil madali itong pakainin ng damo at hindi gaanong magastos.
copy.bis: Daghang Pilipino ang nag-atiman og kanding sa bakuran kay sayon kini pakan-on og sagbot ug dili mahal.

assignedReviews.reason: The card is not living things interacting through competition or predation.

copy.en: Goats live together in a herd because they feel much safer when they stick together as a group.
copy.tl: Ang mga kambing ay sama-samang nabubuhay sa isang kawan dahil mas ligtas ang pakiramdam nila kapag magkakasama.
copy.bis: Ang mga kanding magkuyog nga nagpuyo sa usa ka panon tungod kay mas luwas ang ilang pamati kung magtapok sila.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: calcium to keep your bones strong
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that goat milk contains calcium for strong bones, which touches on the skeletal system, but it does not describe how the skeletal system (or any other body system) works. It is a nutrition fact, not an explanation of system function.

copy.en: Goat milk is a nutritious drink packed with calcium to keep your bones strong.
copy.tl: Ang gatas ng kambing ay masustansyang inumin na mayaman sa kalsiyum para sa malulusog na buto.
copy.bis: Ang gatas sa kanding usa ka masustansya nga ilimnon nga dato sa calcium alang sa lig-on nga bukog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Before the maximum height, the object is ascending and its height increases; after the peak, it is descending and its height decreases.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify examples of everyday situations that demonstrate: a. kinetic energy being transformed to potential energy, and b. potential energy being transformed to kinetic energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card only describes changes in projectile height before and after the peak. It never mentions kinetic energy, potential energy, or their transformation, so it does not directly support identifying energy transformations.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Before the maximum height, the object is ascending and its height increases; after the peak, it is descending and its height decreases.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and identify sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy at school, at home and in the local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about projectile motion and height changes, with no reference to light, sound, or heat energy sources or uses, which is the subject of G4-F-10.

copy.en:
What happens to a projectile's height before and after its peak?

Before the maximum height, the object is ascending and its height increases; after the peak, it is descending and its height decreases.
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari sa taas ng projectile bago at pagkatapos ng tuktok?

Bago ang maximum height, umaakyat ang bagay at tumataas ang height nito; pagkatapos ng tuktok, bumababa ito at bumababa ang height.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang mahitabo sa taas sa projectile sa wala pa ug pagkahuman sa kinatas-an?

Sa wala pa ang maximum height, mosaka ang butang ug motaas ang height; pagkahuman sa kinatas-an, mokanaog kini ug mokunhod ang height.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Gold sinks in water because its density (19.3 g/cm³) is very high compared to water!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions density as a reason for sinking, which is related to heaviness/material, but it does not explore or describe the listed factors (size, shape, heaviness, material, surface texture) affecting object movement.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Gold sinks in water because its density (19.3 g/cm³) is very high compared to water!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: Density relates to mass and volume, but the card does not describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space; it only states a density comparison.

copy.en: Gold sinks in water because its density (19.3 g/cm³) is very high compared to water! Even treasure drops to the bottom.
copy.tl: Lumulubog ang ginto (gold) sa tubig dahil napakataas ng densidad nito (19.3 g/cm³) kaysa tubig! Kahit yaman, lumulubog!
copy.bis: Molunod ang bulawan (gold) sa tubig kay taas kaayo ang density niini (19.3 g/cm³) kaysa tubig! Bisan bahandi, molunod!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Standing tall with your head up makes you look more confident to others
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses posture and confidence, not the workings of the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory systems. It does not describe any body system or how it works, so it provides no direct instructional support for G4-L-1.

copy.en: Standing tall with your head up makes you look more confident to others — scientists say good posture can even help you feel better too.
copy.tl: Kapag tuwid ang tindig mo at nakaangat ang ulo, mukha kang mas may kumpiyansa — sabi pa ng mga siyentista, ang magandang postura ay nakakatulong para mas maging maganda ang pakiramdam mo.
copy.bis: Kon tul-id ang imong tindog ug nagbayaw ang ulo, mukita ka nga mas kompiyante — matod pa sa mga siyentista, ang maayong postura makatabang sab nga mas maayo ang imong pamati.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: keep your head up, back straight, and don't slouch as you move
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives posture advice for walking, which touches on muscular/skeletal involvement, but it does not describe how any human body system works. It lacks the functional explanation required by G4-L-1.

copy.en:
Is good posture only for sitting?

No! You need good posture while walking too — keep your head up, back straight, and don't slouch as you move.
copy.tl:
Postura lang ba kapag nakaupo ang kailangan?

Hindi! Kailangan din ang magandang postura kapag naglalakad — itaas ang ulo, tuwid ang likod, at huwag yumuko.
copy.bis:
Postura ra ba kung naglingkod ang gikinahanglan?

Dili! Kinahanglan usab ang maayong postura kung naglakaw — ipataas ang ulo, tul-ira ang likod, ug ayaw pagtikuko.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Keep your computer or tablet at eye level! If it's too low, your neck gets cramped from looking down — raising it keeps your back and neck straight.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an ergonomic tip about screen height and posture, mentioning neck and back, but it does not describe how the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory systems work. It only tangentially relates to the skeletal/muscular systems through posture, without teaching their function.

copy.en: Keep your computer or tablet at eye level! If it's too low, your neck gets cramped from looking down — raising it keeps your back and neck straight.
copy.tl: Itapat ang computer o tablet mo sa antas ng mata mo! Kapag masyadong mababa, naiipit ang leeg mo sa pagtingin pababa — itaas ito para tuwid ang likod at leeg.
copy.bis: Ibutang ang imong computer o tablet sa lebel sa imong mata! Kung ubos kaayo, maipit ang imong liog sa pagtan-aw ubos — ipataas kini aron tul-id ang likod ug liog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Stand up and stretch every so often to rest your muscles
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions muscles and resting them, but it does not describe how the muscular system (or any other body system) works. It is a health/ergonomics tip about taking stretch breaks, not an explanation of muscle function, contraction, or system operation.

copy.en: Even with good posture, sitting still too long isn't healthy. Stand up and stretch every so often to rest your muscles — like a refresh for your body.
copy.tl: Kahit maganda ang postura mo, hindi mabuting matagal kang nakaupo nang hindi gumagalaw. Tumayo't mag-stretch paminsan-minsan para makapahinga ang mga kalamnan mo.
copy.bis: Bisan maayo ang imong postura, dili maayo nga dugay kang naglingkod nga walay lihok. Tindog ug mag-unat matag-usa aron makapahulay ang imong kaunoran.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sitting up straight keeps your spine healthy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the spine and back pain, which are part of the skeletal system, but it does not describe how the skeletal system (or any other listed system) works. It is a posture/health tip, not an explanation of system function.

copy.en:
Why does sitting up straight matter?

Sitting up straight keeps your spine healthy, while slouching often can lead to back pain over time!
copy.tl:
Bakit mahalaga ang tuwid na pag-upo?

Ang tuwid na pag-upo ay nakakatulong sa malusog na gulugod, samantalang ang madalas na pagyuko ay maaaring magdulot ng sakit sa likod sa paglaon!
copy.bis:
Nganong hinungdanon ang pagtul-id og lingkod?

Ang tul-id nga paglingkod makatabang nga himsog ang gulugod, samtang ang kanunay nga pagkubo mahimong moresulta og sakit sa likod sa kadugayan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Tiny muscles in your skin pull tight, making each hair stand up
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a specific muscle action (goosebumps) but does not describe how the muscular system works as a body system, nor any of the other listed systems. It shares the word 'muscles' but gives no systemic explanation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Tiny muscles in your skin pull tight, making each hair stand up
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: Goosebumps are a response, but the card does not teach the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce) as a general concept. It only gives one isolated physiological example without connecting it to the competency's skill.

copy.en:
What actually causes goosebumps?

Tiny muscles in your skin pull tight, making each hair stand up — that's what causes goosebumps.
copy.tl:
Ano ang sanhi ng kilabot?

Ang kilabot ay nangyayari kapag humihila ang maliliit na kalamnan sa balat, kaya tumitindig ang mga balahibo.
copy.bis:
Unsa'y hinungdan sa kurirot?

Ang kurirot mahitabo kon mobira ang gagmay nga unod sa panit, busa motindog ang mga balhibo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It listens to signals from satellites in the sky and measures their travel time!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify practical applications of electromagnetic radiation, such as radio waves used in telecommunications, and x-rays and gamma rays in medicine
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes GPS using satellite signals but never identifies these signals as electromagnetic radiation or radio waves, nor does it connect GPS to the practical applications of EMR as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It listens to signals from satellites in the sky and measures their travel time!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe electromagnetic radiation (EMR) as energy that is created by the vibrations of electrically charged particles which allows it to travel through materials or space as transverse waves
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions satellite signals but does not describe electromagnetic radiation as energy created by vibrating charged particles or as transverse waves, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It listens to signals from satellites in the sky and measures their travel time!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to explore and describe some ways to use movement, sound, and light to send information between two people
assignedReviews.reason: The card involves sending information via satellite signals, but it does not explore or describe ways to use movement, sound, or light to send information between two people as required by the competency.

copy.en:
How does your phone's GPS know where you are?

It listens to signals from satellites in the sky and measures their travel time! It needs at least four satellites to be perfectly accurate.
copy.tl:
Paano nalalaman ng GPS ng telepono kung nasaan ka?

Nakikinig ito sa hudyat ng mga satellite sa langit at sinusukat ang oras ng pagdating! Kailangan nito ng kahit apat na satellite para maging tumpak.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagsayod sa GPS sa telepono kung asa ka?

Maminaw kini sa signal sa mga satellite sa langit ug sukdon ang oras sa pag-abot! Kinahanglan kini ug labing menos upat ka satellite aron tukma.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A grasshopper grows through three stages -- egg, nymph, and adult -- this is called incomplete metamorphosis.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the life-cycle stages of a grasshopper but does not use a flow chart or compare stages across animals as required by G4-L-5. The format-required activity (flow chart comparison) is absent, so the card is at most related_only.

copy.en: A grasshopper grows through three stages -- egg, nymph, and adult -- this is called incomplete metamorphosis.
copy.tl: Dumaraan ang tipaklong sa tatlong yugto -- itlog, nimpa, at matanda -- tinatawag itong di-buong metamorphosis.
copy.bis: Moagi ang apan sa tulo ka ang-ang -- itlog, nympha, ug hamtong -- gitawag kining dili kompletong metamorphosis.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A grasshopper grows through incomplete metamorphosis — it goes from egg, to nymph, to adult insect.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the life-cycle stages of a grasshopper but does not use a flow chart, nor does it compare stages across different animals as required by the competency. It provides related life-cycle content but no direct instructional support for the specified skill or format.

copy.en: A grasshopper grows through incomplete metamorphosis — it goes from egg, to nymph, to adult insect.
copy.tl: Dumadaan ang tipaklong sa di-ganap na metamorposis — mula itlog, nimpa, hanggang maging adultong insekto.
copy.bis: Ang apan moagi sa dili-hingpit nga metamorphosis — gikan sa itlog, nymph, hangtod mahimong hamtong nga insekto.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Grasslands go by different names around the world
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a list or draw up a table with examples of animals and plants in a particular habitat, such as a garden, rice field, seashore, and mangrove swamp
assignedReviews.reason: The card only gives alternative names for grasslands (prairie, savanna). It does not list or tabulate examples of animals and plants in a particular habitat, which is the required action of G4-L-4.

copy.en: Grasslands go by different names around the world — prairie in North America and savanna in Africa.
copy.tl: Ang mga grassland ay may iba't ibang pangalan sa buong mundo — prairie sa North America at savanna sa Africa.
copy.bis: Ang mga grassland adunay lain-laing ngalan sa tibuok kalibutan — prairie sa North America ug savanna sa Africa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earth's gravity reaches all the way to the Moon
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes gravity acting on the Moon, not on objects on Earth as required by the competency. It does not explicitly identify gravity as a non-contact force or address predictable effects on Earth materials/objects.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: keeping it orbiting around us
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the effects of gravity to the motion of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the Moon's orbital motion due to gravity, not the motion of an object on Earth. The competency requires observing/describing gravity's effects on an object's motion, which this card does not directly support.

copy.en: Earth's gravity reaches all the way to the Moon, keeping it orbiting around us!
copy.tl: Nararating ng grabidad ng Lupa ang Buwan, kaya patuloy itong umiikot sa atin!
copy.bis: Nakaabot ang grabidad sa Yuta hangtod sa Bulan, mao nga padayon kini naglibot kanato!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You can't see gravity, but you definitely feel its pull every single day!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that gravity is invisible and that its pull is felt. It does not identify gravity as a non-contact force, nor does it describe predictable effects on materials/objects, which are the core requirements of G5-F-4.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You can't see gravity, but you definitely feel its pull every single day!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the effects of gravity to the motion of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions feeling gravity's pull but does not describe any observable effect of gravity on the motion of an object, which is the focus of G5-F-6.

copy.en: You can't see gravity, but you definitely feel its pull every single day!
copy.tl: Hindi mo makikita ang grabidad, pero ramdam mo ang pull niya araw-araw!
copy.bis: Dili nimo makita ang grabidad, pero mabati nimo ang iyang bira matag adlaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The scientist Isaac Newton helped explain how gravity works!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies Isaac Newton as a scientist who explained gravity, but the competency requires identifying a scientist and their invention/s. Gravity is a discovery, not an invention, and the card does not mention any invention. Thus it only shares the broad subject of a famous scientist, not the specific skill of identifying an invention.

copy.en:
Who helped explain how gravity works?

The scientist Isaac Newton helped explain how gravity works!
copy.tl:
Sino ang tumulong magpaliwanag kung paano gumagana ang grabidad?

Ang siyentipikong si Isaac Newton ang tumulong magpaliwanag kung paano gumagana ang grabidad!
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang mitabang sa pagpasabot kung unsaon paglihok sa grabidad?

Ang siyentipiko nga si Isaac Newton mitabang sa pagpasabot kung unsaon paglihok sa grabidad!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A helium balloon rising doesn't mean gravity turned off!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: predict and explain whether heavier objects will fall faster than lighter objects due to the force of gravity
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that gravity still acts on a rising balloon, but the competency requires predicting/explaining whether heavier objects fall faster than lighter objects due to gravity. The card does not address the comparison of falling speeds of objects of different weights, so it only shares the general topic of gravity without directly supporting the specific skill.

copy.en: A helium balloon rising doesn't mean gravity turned off! A larger upward force from the air is just winning for a while.
copy.tl: Ang helium balloon na umaakyat ay hindi ibig sabihin na nawala ang gravity! Mas malakas lang pansamantala ang upward force ng hangin.
copy.bis: Ang helium balloon nga mosaka dili pasabot nga wala na ang gravity! Mas kusog lang temporaryo ang upward force sa hangin.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Gray's monitor lizard is one of the very few monitor lizards that eats fruit as a major part of its diet.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card provides a fact about a specific animal's diet (fruit-eating) but does not group the animal into herbivore, carnivore, or omnivore categories, nor does it teach the classification skill. It is related vocabulary (food eaten) but does not directly support the competency's action of grouping animals by food type.

copy.en:
What lizard mainly eats fruit?

Gray's monitor lizard is one of the very few monitor lizards that eats fruit as a major part of its diet.
copy.tl:
Anong butiki ang kumakain ng prutas?

Ang Gray's monitor lizard ay isa sa napakailang monitor lizard na kumakain ng prutas bilang mahalagang bahagi ng kanyang pagkain.
copy.bis:
Unsang butiki ang nakaon og prutas?

Ang Gray's monitor lizard usa sa pipila lang ka monitor lizard nga nakaon og prutas isip importanteng bahin sa iyang pagkaon.
